text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.5% today, extending a two-week slide of 14%, as oil prices softened and geopolitical tensions that might support energy demand showed no sign of resolving into actual supply disruptions. US crude dropped to $82.24 per barrel, down from levels that would have supported higher refining margins earlier this month. While refineries are running at a robust 97.5%, the combination of lower oil prices and high product inventories—217.7 million barrels of gasoline and 105.6 million barrels of diesel in storage—squeezes the profit refiners make on each barrel they process.

The broader headwind is that Middle Eastern tensions (Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, Iranian tankers hitting mines, Ukraine's refinery strikes on Russian assets) remain serious but have not yet created a visible supply crisis or oil price spike that would offset the downward pressure from abundant inventories and softer crude. Traders appear to be pricing in containment rather than escalation.
